name: Money & Tax
blurb: VAT, salary, loan, discount, overtime and tips — the numbers you have to get right.
meta_title: Money & Tax Calculators — VAT, Salary, Loan & Tips
meta_description: Free money and tax calculators: add or remove VAT, convert salary to hourly pay, work out loan EMI, discounts, overtime pay and bill tips. No sign-up.
intro: Six calculators for the money questions that come with a deadline: an invoice that needs VAT added, a job offer that needs comparing, a loan that needs checking, a bill that needs splitting. Each page states its formula and its limits, because a number you cannot check is not much use.
body:
Why these calculators show the formula

Financial mistakes are rarely arithmetic mistakes — they are direction mistakes. Adding VAT and removing VAT need different operations. Percentage increase and percentage decrease do not cancel out. Overtime is paid on a base rate that may or may not include shift premiums. When the formula is on the page, you can see which direction the tool went and catch a wrong assumption before it reaches an invoice or a payslip.

What these tools do not do

None of them estimate tax you owe. Income tax, national insurance, social security and pension rules depend on where you live, your household and your employment status, and a generic deduction would be wrong for most visitors. The salary calculator converts gross pay between periods and says so; the VAT calculator applies the rate you choose and tells you to confirm that rate with your tax authority. For anything filed with a government, use the official calculator.

Where to start

If you are invoicing, start with the VAT calculator. If you are comparing a job offer or a contract, start with the salary calculator and then check overtime. If you are borrowing, the loan calculator's amortisation schedule shows how much of an early repayment goes to principal, which is the number that actually decides whether prepaying is worth it.

name: Everyday Calculators
blurb: Percentages and BMI — two numbers that come up constantly and are easy to get wrong.
meta_title: Everyday Calculators — Percentage and BMI Tools
meta_description: Free everyday calculators: solve any percentage question with the formula shown, and check body mass index with the healthy weight range for your height.
intro: Two calculators that cover a surprising share of daily questions: what a percentage actually means in the sentence you are reading, and what a body mass index number does and does not tell you. Both explain their method rather than only returning a figure.
body:
Percentages: the sentence is the formula

Almost every percentage mistake comes from answering the wrong question. 'What is 15% of 80' is multiplication. '15 is what percent of 80' is division. 'A price rose from 80 to 92' is a change calculation on the original value. 'A price of 92 includes 15% tax' requires division by 1.15, not subtraction of 15%. The percentage calculator has a mode for each, and prints the formula it used so you can confirm which one you needed.

BMI: a screening number, not a diagnosis

Body mass index is a population-level screening tool. It is cheap, reproducible and useful across large groups, and it cannot distinguish muscle from fat. The calculator shows the WHO bands and the healthy weight range for your height so the number can be interpreted in context, and it is explicit that athletes, older adults, children and some ethnic groups need different measures or thresholds.

Use them together

Both tools are often the first step in a bigger question. A percentage result may feed a discount, a VAT calculation or a loan comparison; a BMI result may lead to a conversation with a clinician. The related tools on each page point to the next step.

name: Dates & Time
blurb: Days between dates, exact age, and converting times across time zones.
meta_title: Date & Time Calculators — Duration, Age, Time Zones
meta_description: Calculate days between two dates, exact age in years, months and days, and convert times across time zones with daylight saving handled correctly.
intro: Three tools for the questions that trip people up because calendars are not uniform: months vary in length, leap years add a day, daylight saving moves an hour twice a year, and contracts disagree about whether the start date counts.
body:
Dates are not arithmetic

Adding 30 days is not the same as adding one month. A notice period starting on 31 January has no 31 February to land on, which is why legal counting rules exist and why the inclusive/exclusive choice changes the answer by a day. The date duration calculator gives the result in years, months and days as well as in raw days and weeks, and it lets you pick the counting convention instead of guessing.

Time zones are rules, not offsets

A fixed offset such as UTC+1 is not a time zone. Europe/London switches between GMT and BST, and the transition dates differ from those in the United States, so the London–New York gap is five hours for most of the year and four hours for a couple of weeks in spring and autumn. The time zone converter uses the browser's IANA database, so the answer is correct for the specific date you select — including those awkward weeks.

Age is a legal question as well as a personal one

Age in completed years on a specific date decides eligibility for exams, visas, pensions and school entry. The age calculator uses the years-months-days method that forms ask for, handles 29 February birthdays explicitly, and can measure age on any future date rather than only today.

name: Text & Code
blurb: Word counts, text case, diffs and JSON — clean up text before it goes anywhere.
meta_title: Text & Code Tools — Word Count, Case, Diff, JSON
meta_description: Count words and characters, convert text case, compare two texts for differences and format or validate JSON — all in the browser, with nothing uploaded.
intro: Four utilities for the last five minutes before something is submitted, published or deployed: hitting a character limit, fixing a headline typed in caps, confirming only one line changed, and finding out why a payload will not parse.
body:
Limits, and which one applies

Forms specify character limits, sometimes with spaces and sometimes without, and word processors disagree about hyphens and numbers. The word counter shows both character figures at once so you do not have to guess, along with reading time and the words you are repeating most.

Case is a formatting decision with consequences

Title case has rules, not just capital letters — short prepositions stay lowercase unless they open the title. Developer naming conventions are stricter still: kebab-case for URLs and CSS because search engines treat hyphens as separators, snake_case for JSON keys and database columns, camelCase for JavaScript variables. The case converter handles all of them and preserves line breaks, so a whole document converts at once.

Diffs and JSON catch what eyes miss

Human attention follows meaning, so a deleted 'not' can pass a proofread. A line-based diff marks every change in red and green and counts them. JSON has no comments and no tolerance: one trailing comma breaks the whole document, which is why the formatter reports the exact line and character rather than a generic parse error.

name: PDF & Image
blurb: Merge PDFs, compress images, make PDFs, convert formats — without uploading.
meta_title: PDF & Image Tools — Merge, Compress, Convert Locally
meta_description: Merge PDFs, compress JPG and PNG images, turn photos into a PDF, convert JPG to PNG and DOCX to PDF. Everything runs in your browser with no upload.
intro: Five file tools built around one rule: your documents never leave your device. Merging a bank statement or compressing a passport scan normally means uploading it to someone else's server and trusting their retention policy. Here the work happens in browser memory.
body:
Why client-side file tools are different

Upload-based converters have to store your file at least temporarily, and free tiers often come with page limits, watermarks or waiting queues. Client-side tools read the file into browser memory, transform it, and hand back a download. There is no upload step, no server copy and no queue. It also means the tools keep working offline, which matters on a train or on a locked-down network.

What that trade-off costs

Honesty matters more here than anywhere else. Very large files are limited by your device's memory rather than a server farm, so a phone will struggle where a laptop copes. Password-protected PDFs are not unlocked. The Word to PDF converter rebuilds text rather than rendering Word's layout engine, so complex designs lose their formatting. Each page says what it does not do, because a misleading conversion wastes more time than a clear refusal.

A practical order of operations

If a combined document is too large to email, compress or downscale the images first, then build or merge the PDF. Merging and then compressing is harder to control, because you can no longer tune the quality of each source image.
